cells.tense: You are in the shared gladness right now, and the pen is in your hand.
cells.ask: Tell one person something good that's true today, not to lift them, just because it's true, and let that be the whole point.
cells.core:
Your gladness has a direction and you don't need a crowd for it to be real. You move toward what's genuinely good and you bring people into it because it holds better that way. The celebration isn't the reward waiting at the end. It's part of how the thing you're building gets its meaning.

That's what's running well: you can sit with one person and let something good be true out loud, and that's the whole event. You're not performing it, you're in it, and the people around you can feel the difference. What you're free to feed next is the quieter version — the small moment, no occasion, nobody watching, and it still counts.
cells.sheetLine: Your gladness has a direction, and you bring people into it.
cells.verb: raising joy together until it multiplies
cells.place: a place where the pull toward what you actually want can be felt

cells.tense: You will be bracing for a moment that has not arrived, writing the celebration before it is earned.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're making and finish one small piece of it today, with nobody watching and nothing said about it afterward.
cells.core:
You're running ahead of the thing you're trying to make. The celebration gets planned before it's earned — who hears about it, how it lands, what it will mean — and the picturing has taken the place of the making. The joy is carrying weight it wasn't built for, holding up a future instead of marking a present.

Wanting it to mean something with people isn't wrong. But the push spends the warmth before it arrives, and the building is what is actually being avoided. A quiet day of real work would feed you more than another round of imagining how it will go. Pick the smallest piece and let it be small, and let nobody know yet.
cells.sheetLine: You're planning the celebration before there's anything to celebrate.

cells.tense: You have stopped showing up to the rooms that used to be yours, and you are standing outside them now.
cells.ask: Go sit in one group or room you used to belong to, once, with no agenda, and see what's still there for you.
cells.core:
Your gladness stopped going out loud in company, and that sharing is what's missing. You can still feel the pull toward what you want — that part is intact — but you stopped moving toward it around other people. The inner work is happening alone, and it needs the shared version to finish itself, and the shared version isn't happening.

What's absent isn't the wish for any of it. It's the return. One room where the thing gets said out loud around other people, one ordinary hour of it, and you find out whether it's still yours. No performance, no arrival, nothing announced. Just go and sit in it once and let that be the experiment.
cells.sheetLine: The pull is still there. You stopped saying it around people.

cells.tense: You are already the one lifting the room, and you keep calling it something else.
cells.ask: Catch one moment this week where the warmth in a room came from you, and say it to yourself in one sentence, no reasons added.
cells.core:
You're the one lifting the room. The thing you notice, the thing you say when the energy dips, the way you show up — that's you doing the work of shared joy, and you keep filing it under the group's mood or somebody else's doing. Meanwhile the pull toward what you actually want is right there in that choosing, and nothing about it is getting read as yours.

That mislabel costs you something. If the warmth counts as the room's, it tells you nothing about what you're steering toward. But it's yours. You're the one who knows what's worth raising together, and putting your name on that isn't taking credit. It's just where the fact already sits.

attempts.check: The Celebration card's record says joy wants to be shared and meaning is found in celebrating together, but the seat is Inspiration — the draw toward what's genuinely desired. The unsupported claim in my draft is that this person already knows what they want and the celebration is the thing that's blocked; the record doesn't say that, it only names the capacity. A reader could reasonably say the problem isn't celebration at all, it's that they don't know what star to steer by. The ask survives being wrong: sharing something small and true with one person works whether the block is in the wanting or in the sharing. The sentence that serves me more than them is any version of 'you know what you want' — that's my invention, not the map, and it goes.
